headline: HSC and equivalent results deferred to October 31
summary: Originally scheduled for October 29, the results for over 1.2 million candidates will now be published two days later.
details: The results of this year’s HSC and equivalent examinations will be published on October 31, two days later than the previously announced date of October 29.
The Bangladesh Inter-Education Board Coordination Committee announced the revised date in a notice issued yesterday.
The results will be announced at 11:00 am at the International Mother Language Institute in Dhaka and will be available simultaneously at educational institutions and online.
The notice was signed by committee president Prof Syed Akhtaruzzaman, who also serves as the chairman of the Dhaka Education Board.
Students can access their results through their respective education boards’ websites, their institutions, or via SMS.
Applications for re-scrutiny will be accepted online from November 1 to 7 via the education boards’ websites.
A total of 1,270,583 candidates registered for this year’s HSC and equivalent examinations across 11 education boards.

headline_marked: Police to [[crack down on drug and teen gang kingpins]]
headline: Police to crack down on drug and teen gang kingpins
summary: Additional IGP Md Sayedur Rahman announces a zero-tolerance policy against drug networks and juvenile gangs during a crime review meeting.
details: Bangladesh Police have been instructed to identify and take strict action against the alleged masterminds behind drug networks and teenage gangs.
Additional IGP (Crime and Operations) Md Sayedur Rahman stated that the police maintain a zero-tolerance policy towards these groups during a monthly crime review meeting at Police Headquarters.
Officers were urged to perform their duties with honesty and professionalism, treat the public humanely, and investigate robbery cases promptly to ensure justice.
Regarding rape cases, the Additional IGP emphasized that investigations must be closely supervised to improve conviction rates.
The meeting also reviewed the overall crime situation in September, including murder, banditry, abduction, and attacks on police.
The review session was attended by police commissioners, range deputy inspectors general, and district police superintendents via video link.
caption:
